problem:
For the sets $X={k,m,n}$ and $Z=X\times X,$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- ${k}^{2}\in Z$
- $(k,n,m)\in Z$
- $(m,n)\in Z$

feedback.problem:
For the sets $X={f,g,h}$ and $Z=X\times X,$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- $(f,g)\in Z$
- $(f,g,h)\in Z$
- $(h,h)\in Z$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $X\times X$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $X$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $X.$

In this case, the schematic for ${X}^{2}=X\times X$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040355/assets/1718bd6f3f2eaa8dd8fe581b0d938b3b5f1928d5e56a11a324f145e7a481fabe.png)

Hence, the set $Z=X\times X$ is given by

$$
Z={(f,f),(f,g),(f,h),(g,f),(g,g),(g,h),(h,f),(h,g),(h,h)}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
